evidence: I walked every criterion (2 gates, 11 functional, 5 polish, 5 visual likert) for a concrete observable outcome, durable evidence, distinctive probes and decidability. STRENGTHS: every board and message step uses suffixed records. The seeded facts quoted in criteria match seed_data.json: Platform Engineer Applied Greta/Ade/Marco and Screen Priya/Samuel; Noor's note; Lena's unread count of 1 (read_count 2 of 3, and message 3 is by Farah); Noor's Platform Engineer application in Interview/Infrastructure and Product Designer in Applied/Design; Tomas's Data Analyst application in Screen/Finance Systems. Persistence uses restart_app and re-reads several recorded items in a fresh context, which satisfies lesson 15. The timed observations in functional/prompt.md:29 and polish/prompt.md:18 define all of the following, which satisfies lessons 7 and 14: t0 is recorded only after a successful trigger; polling runs every 500 ms; an attempt is void only if it errored before t0 or the trigger failed; at most two repeats; met=false is final; negatives are watched for the full window. app_context.md tells the judge to hold modifier keys during the click. No judge file contains a public internet address (a grep for non-local URLs returned nothing). Suites run sequentially (test.sh:207, --max-concurrent-agent 1), so the exact count deltas in hro_unread_seen are decidable. INSTANCES FOUND: (1) BLOCKING. tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:85, hro_manager_roles. The setup leaves exactly 'two in Interview'. Ingrid's ordered steps are 'move an Interview card to Offer, to Hired and back to Offer; re-order cards in Offer or Interview'. At that point Interview and Offer each hold one card, so no re-order is possible. The Bar still requires that 'Ingrid's late-stage moves, re-orders ... all succeed'. functional/prompt.md:11 requires the steps 'in its order', and prompt.md:33 says 'A step you skipped or did differently fails that criterion'. The leg cannot be decided for a correct app. The scripted golden (workspace.cjs, around line 132) sets this up through API fixtures and does not follow the criterion's order, so it does not cover this case. (2) tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:76, hro_undo_activity: 'Capture the first undo request for the replays', which is the undo of V's single move. The golden undo route (src/index.js:351) refuses any action_id that is not the caller's latest action not yet undone, with 'There is nothing of yours to undo.' The replays in steps 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8 therefore reuse a stale action id and are refused for a reason unrelated to the rule under test (repeat undo, or a colleague changed a card). The server-side colleague-change and undo-once rules are then proven only by the UI leg. An app whose UI hides Undo client-side while its server would still apply the undo passes. The fresh-value rule in prompt.md:25 covers card versions only, and its exclusion ('changed or out of date does not count') does not mention a stale undo id. (3) 'Try' legs that cannot be expressed, in hro_moves (judge.toml:40) and the closest-request replay rule (prompt.md:25): 'try A Interview to Hired / Interview to Applied', 'try to reopen C to Screen', 'try to reopen E to Applied and to Interview'. The brief lets an app offer only one-stage forward/back controls and a Reopen with no target stage, because reopening goes 'exactly to that stage and nowhere else' (hireops_rules.md:48-51). For such an app, neither the UI nor any request shape can express the forbidden target. The judge is told to 'replay the closest observed request with that change', but the task does not say what to do when the change cannot be expressed. If the judge adds a field the server ignores, the server may reopen or advance the card legally and the conforming app fails. If the judge records a skipped step, it also fails. NOTES, NOT BLOCKING: hro_pol_failed_send (polish judge.toml:52) checks 'sent once' without rereading from the server in a fresh context or after a reload, which weakens the durable evidence against a duplicate send queued by an outbox. hro_candidate's 'board positions' in responses has no observable definition. The visual likert rows are subjective by design, have anchors for 1 to 5 and use the accepted format.
counterexample: A conforming app that fails: a correct, golden-equivalent app graded on hro_manager_roles. After Ingrid moves one of the two Interview cards to Offer, then Hired, then back to Offer, Interview and Offer each hold one card. The 're-order cards in Offer or Interview' step cannot be performed in order, so the criterion (weight 4 of 61 functional) scores 0. A second conforming app fails hro_moves: it has forward/back buttons and a one-click Reopen with no target stage. The judge replays 'reopen C to Screen' by adding a stage field the server ignores. The server legally reopens C to Applied, and the leg 'refused with the card unchanged' is recorded as failed. A broken app that passes: its server's /undo ignores colleague changes, while its UI hides Undo once it sees the board has changed. The UI leg sends nothing, and the replay of the first captured undo request (V's stale action id) is refused as 'nothing to undo'. Steps 4, 6, 7 and 8 of hro_undo_activity therefore pass without the server enforcing the rule.
suggested_fix: In hro_manager_roles, set up three cards in Interview (or have Ingrid move a second card into Offer before re-ordering) so that two cards share a late stage when Ingrid re-orders. In hro_undo_activity, have every undo replay resend the undo request that the UI just made, or would make, for the move under test, with its current action identifier, and say that a refusal citing only a stale or missing undo target does not count. In hro_moves and the replay rule, say that when neither the UI nor any observed request shape can express a forbidden target (a skipped stage or a wrong reopen stage), the leg passes because the move cannot be made, provided the allowed move succeeded as the control and the card is unchanged.
